values: Plain-language tracker for security, performance, MFA, payments, and UI/UX work. Planned period: Monday, 12-Oct-2026 to Thursday, 31-Dec-2026.

Planning assumptions:
• This is a two-resource project. Resource 1 focuses on backend, security, cloud, and performance. Resource 2 focuses on frontend, product, identity, and QA. Some tasks are shared.
• Cybersecurity work covers encryption, decryption access, key management, password hashing, and security testing.
• Node.js performance work covers a baseline, load testing, and optimization.
• MFA requires choosing/configuring a domain or identity provider before implementation.
• UI/UX is outsourced. If started Monday, 12-Oct-2026, the initial design delivery is expected around Monday, 26-Oct-2026.
• Payment gateway remains a decision item until the business confirms that paid transactions are needed.
• Final plan review is scheduled for Thursday, 31-Dec-2026.
Confirm the 3-month scope and weekly check-ins
Everyone agrees what will be delivered and when
Use this sheet as the weekly review list
List all personal, login, payment, and medical data
A simple data map shows where each type of data is stored
Include database, S3, logs, backups, and vendors
A short list of risks and fixes is approved
Prioritize problems that could expose user or health data
Protect data while it is moving
HTTPS/TLS is used for browser, API, database, and storage connections
Database, S3 files, and backups use encryption and private access
Keep buckets private and use short-lived download links
Control who can decrypt and view sensitive data
Only approved roles can access decrypted files and records
Add audit logs for sensitive access
New passwords use Argon2id and old hashes migrate after successful login
Login, storage, access control, rate limits, and secrets are tested
Measure current API speed and resource use
Baseline shows response time, CPU, memory, and error rate
The team knows how the API behaves with normal and peak traffic
Use synthetic users and test files
Slow queries, memory issues, and blocking code are improved
Results meet agreed response-time and error-rate targets
Choose the domain or identity provider for MFA
The MFA provider, domain, email/SMS method, and cost are approved
Domain setup is a dependency for this feature
Configure the MFA domain and provider
The staging domain sends and verifies MFA codes successfully
Build MFA login, recovery, and admin controls
Users can enroll, verify, recover, and disable MFA safely
MFA works on common devices and recovery does not weaken security
Test lost phone and backup-code scenarios
Decide whether a payment gateway is needed
Business confirms the payment provider, countries, currencies, and refund rules
Keep this as optional until confirmed
Set up the payment provider in test mode
Sandbox account, webhooks, keys, and test products work
Never use live keys in development
Build checkout, payment status, and refunds
A test payment can be created, confirmed, failed, refunded, and recorded
Verify webhooks instead of trusting the browser
Test payment security and end-to-end flow
Duplicate payments, failed payments, refunds, and webhook retries are handled
Vendor has screens, user journeys, brand direction, and acceptance criteria
Initial screens and user flows are delivered for review
Review and revise the UI/UX design
Approved screens are ready for development handoff
Prepare staging release and user acceptance testing
Security, performance, MFA, payment, and UI/UX work is tested together
Fix UAT issues and complete go-live checklist
Open critical issues are closed and owners approve release
Keep Dec 31 as the final review date
Team records what is done, what remains, and the next priorities
Use actual progress to reset dates
